item.title: Sparking Dynamic, Relativistic Magnetic Reconnection in a Twisted Flux Tube
item.description: arXiv:2610.22653v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Magnetic reconnection around neutron stars (NSs) forms small-scale currents while transferring energy to electron-positron pairs. These dissipating currents cover a wide range of scales, potentially leaving an imprint on time-variable X-ray bursts and pulsed radio emission. We present a reduced, planar model of internal reconnection in a magnetic flux tube with relativistic magnetization, finite resistivity, and strong guide field. Comparing with realistic NS parameters, this model represents the dynamics of a slender magnetic flux tube that is much thinner than the stellar radius. The seed current profile is smooth and does not spontaneously reconnect; instead, a discrete and localized current perturbation is introduced, representing e.g. localized energy release from a NS crust or magnetosphere. Three high-resolution relativistic magnetohydrodynamics simulations are described: one has uniform resistivity and Lundquist number such that reconnection proceeds in the plasmoid-mediated regime; the other two account for the feedback of charge starvation on the resistivity in current layers, where density is depleted; we provide a more general explanation for this depletion. All simulations produce a few dominant magnetic X-points and a secondary Kelvin-Helmholtz instability that excites high-wavenumber currents. We quantify the reconnection rate, the intermittency of dissipation, and the time profile of current spikes. We further present three-dimensional simulations confirming a limited growth of the ideal kink mode in the strong guide field regime. Applications are discussed, including to radio pulse microstructure and current damping below the magnetar surface during an X-ray flare, leading to mass loss and X-ray afterglow.
item.dc:creator: Michael P. Grehan, Christopher Thompson, Bart Ripperda, James R. Beattie

item.title: A Unified Solution to the Low-Mass X-ray Binary Diversity Puzzle: Saturated Magnetic Braking Coupled with Irradiation-Driven Winds
item.description: arXiv:2610.22816v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The standard magnetic braking (MB) model has long failed to explain key properties of low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs)---including their accretion rates, the formation of ultracompact binaries, and orbital expansion---casting doubt on binary evolution and gravitational-wave progenitor predictions. Phenomenological modifications exist, but a unified, physically grounded mechanism has been missing. Here we show that the overlooked coupling between magnetic saturation and irradiation-driven winds (IDW) provides this missing framework. Accretion-powered irradiation enhances the donor wind, which in turn amplifies MB exactly where needed. Our Saturated MB + IDW (SMB+IDW) model simultaneously resolves three outstanding discrepancies with no fine-tuning: (1) it reproduces the full observed distribution of accretion rates across persistent and transient LMXBs; (2) it naturally explains ultracompact X-ray binary formation; and (3) it quantitatively matches the orbital period distribution of descendant millisecond pulsar (MSP) binaries---a critical independent test failed by all previous models. Critically, the SMB+IDW model transforms MB from an externally imposed condition into a self-consistently regulated process tied to the accretion history. By unifying LMXB evolution to MSPs in a single physical picture, our work resolves the long-standing diversity puzzle and establishes a physics-based foundation for next-generation population synthesis, gravitational-wave progenitor predictions, and compact binary interpretation across cosmic time.
item.dc:creator: Zhu-Ling Deng, Xiang-Dong Li, Bo Wang, Philipp Podsiadlowski, Yong Shao, Dong-Dong Liu, Zhan-Wen Han

item.title: Gamma-ray calorimetry of Seyfert winds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23028v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Two stacking analyses with the Fermi Large Area Telescope (LAT) detected GeV emission from radio-quiet Seyferts, one selected by an X-ray ultra-fast outflow (UFO) and one hard-X-ray-bright, with similar luminosities attributed to different mechanisms: wind shocks and the accretion-disk corona. We investigate how efficiently Seyfert outflows convert mechanical power into GeV photons, whether the two detections require distinct mechanisms, and how Seyferts compare with low-ionization nuclear emission-line regions (LINERs). Without new Fermi-LAT data reduction, we homogenize published measurements to 0.1-100 GeV, place local mechanical accelerators on one L_gamma-Edot diagram, and express eta = L_gamma/Edot as a fraction rho of the complete-calorimetry efficiency eta_max ~ 2.5%, inverting rho for the ambient density required by pp losses. Winds from Seyfert active galactic nuclei (AGN) have rho = 0.020 (+0.018/-0.011) for acceleration efficiency 0.1, a factor of ~13.5 below starburst superwinds (rho = 0.26 (+0.37/-0.16)). The difference exceeds a factor of three with probability 0.95 and is independent of acceleration parameters common to both classes; it is conditional on the wind kinetic powers, collapsing only if every wind sits at its minimum launch radius. The implied densities, ~10 and ~100 cm^-3, are consistency values: density, shock radius and speed are degenerate. The two stacking detections agree within a factor of 1.75 in gamma-ray output per unit Eddington luminosity, but the 95% interval, 0.26-24, is too wide to distinguish them. A third stack, of 186 low-luminosity AGN, extends the comparison 1.5 dex lower, ordered by AGN power. GeV detectability of non-jetted AGN is set by the product of mechanical power and calorimetric fraction. LINER outflows fail on power; for the adopted wind energetics, Seyfert UFO winds fail on calorimetry; starburst superwinds succeed on both.
item.dc:creator: Alberto Dom\'inguez (IPARCOS/UC Madrid)

item.title: What can a uniform reflection pipeline establish about supermassive black hole spin? An audit and a corrected analysis of 57 AGN with XMM and NuSTAR
item.description: arXiv:2610.23081v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We audit an automated relativistic-reflection pipeline that fitted one XMM-Newton EPIC-pn and NuSTAR epoch for each of 57 AGN with relxillCp+xillverCp, and repeat the analysis with its failures corrected. The pipeline's apparent constraints were not controlled: Small Window pn backgrounds were never subtracted, the nearest-in-time pairing selected mismatched or nearly empty spectra, single-start fits often stopped short of the minimum, and most fits were inadequate or at a parameter limit. The corrected analysis uses in-window backgrounds, 41 sources with eligible pn--NuSTAR pairs, multi-start fits, bidirectional profiles, criteria fixed in advance and eight model variations. 24 of the 41 reference fits have $p\ge0.01$ and 18 pass all quality checks. Their 90% spin sets comprise 1 two-sided interval (NGC 4051, $0.46\le a_*\le0.93$), 6 lower bounds, 4 upper bounds, 4 disconnected sets and 3 unconstrained profiles. For 10 of the 18 the best fit lies at $i\ge75^\circ$, implausible for type-1 AGN, and most of those constraints disappear when $i\le60^\circ$ is imposed. Only 2 of the 15 constrained sets keep their type both under that limit and with pn restricted to 3--10 keV (an upper bound for Mrk 1040 and a weak lower bound for 1H 0419-577). Simulations show that, with a correct model, the 90% sets contain the true spin in 82--92% of cases without drifting edge-on, but at high inclination one low-spin simulation in six yields a false lower bound. We make no statement about the spin distribution or a spin--jet relation.
item.dc:creator: K. Balasubramaniam, H. -K. Chang, {\L}. Stawarz

item.title: Maximal efficiency of geometric beaming and polarization of highly super-Eddington X-ray sources
item.description: arXiv:2610.23089v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Geometric beaming is an often invoked explanation for the apparent super-Eddington luminosities of ultraluminous X-ray sources. It is a natural consequence of the geometrically thick envelope that is expected to surround the inner accretion disk in the super-Eddington accretion regime; as the radiation can only freely escape through a narrow funnel-shaped cavity, the flux along the funnel axis is enhanced. A fraction of the photons will nevertheless escape the funnel cavity at larger angles, reducing the effectiveness of the beaming. To explore the limits of geometric beaming, we performed Monte Carlo simulations of conservative radiative transfer in an infinitely optically thick funnel while accounting for polarization. We discovered that the beaming becomes inefficient when the funnel opening angle is small $(\lesssim15^\circ$) because the photons tend to remain trapped within the cavity until they reach the upper edge of the funnel where they can escape at larger angles. For most of the photons to escape a narrow funnel through a small solid angle, the funnel has to be unrealistically long. Consequently, geometric beaming could at most boost the apparent luminosity by a factor of a few dozen in our idealized simulations. While larger boost factors on the order of $\sim$100 are possible for funnels with a length of $\gtrsim10^5$ Schwarzschild radii, this requires very narrow opening angles of $\lesssim3^\circ$. Additionally, we found that aberration due to mildly relativistic velocities does not significantly change this result. The maximal polarization degree of light reflected by the funnel remained on the order of a few percent for face-on sources and $\lesssim10\%$ for edge-on sources.
item.dc:creator: Varpu Ahlberg, Alexandra Veledina, Eugene Churazov, Ildar Khabibullin

item.title: Ranking Prompt--Plateau Correlations in Gamma-Ray Bursts with Symbolic Regression
item.description: arXiv:2610.23155v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Gamma-ray burst (GRB) correlations probe central engines, relativistic outflows, and radiation processes. The Dainotti relation is an anticorrelation between the X-ray plateau luminosity $L_a$ and rest-frame plateau duration $T_a^{\rm rest}$. We use symbolic regression to compare it with other low-dimensional correlations in 251 GRBs with Swift-XRT plateau properties and Swift-BAT prompt-emission parameters. We perform a Dainotti-guided search, in which $\log T_a^{\rm rest}$ is always present, and an unrestricted search over subsets of at most three variables. The guided search recovers the Dainotti dependence; a D'Agostini fit gives $\log L_a=(51.92\pm0.30)-(1.31\pm0.09)\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with intrinsic scatter $\sigma_{\rm int}=0.82\pm0.05$ dex. In the unrestricted ranking of 377 feature subsets, the classical Dainotti relation remains competitive, within the top $\sim25\%$ of the tested search spaces. The highest-ranked screened expression is $\log L_a\approx0.855\log L_{\rm peak}-0.782\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with RMSE $\approx0.46$ and $R^2\approx0.88$. The highest-ranked runs repeatedly reduce to this prompt--plateau structure, without retaining additional spectral, absorption, or afterglow-shape variables. A direct regression gives $\log L_a=4.718+0.776\log L_{\rm peak}-0.805\log T_a^{\rm rest}$, with $R_{\rm P}=0.91$ for 246 bursts. An errors-in-variables refit gives consistent coefficients. After removing shared luminosity-distance dependence, the relation retains non-negligible explanatory power ($R^2\approx0.62$), consistent with a possible intrinsic component. Restricted Monte Carlo null tests give $p\approx0.01$. Plateau luminosity therefore shows a coupled dependence on prompt luminosity and plateau duration.
item.dc:creator: Fatemeh Rastegarnia, Rahim Moradi, Brwa Shukur Ismael, Mohsen Asaadi, Yu Wang

item.title: The Dancing Bonfire: An Unusual Persistent X-ray Source in M81 Exhibiting Recurrent Luminous Flares
item.description: arXiv:2610.23339v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Short-timescale X-ray variability provides a direct probe of unstable accretion onto compact objects, yet extragalactic X-ray binaries (XRBs) with recurrent flaring remain largely unexplored. Here we present a detailed X-ray study of M81F4 (2CXO J095524.2+690957), a persistently luminous X-ray source towards M81 that exhibits recurrent short X-ray flares. Based on multi-mission X-ray observations spanning two decades, it is found that M81F4 remains persistently bright at $L_{0.5-8.0\rm~keV}\sim10^{38}-10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, while producing flares lasting a few hundred seconds and reaching peak luminosities of a few $10^{39}\rm~erg~s^{-1}$, with an observed mean (minimum) recurrence time of $\sim0.5$ day ($\sim$6 ks). The stacked flare profile shows a rapid rise followed by a slower decay, but no significant hardness evolution. Spectral analysis reveals that both the flare and non-flare states are dominated by a hard power-law continuum, with evidence of highly ionized Fe lines in the non-flare state spectrum. These properties disfavor classical Type I and Type II bursts and have no close analog among known XRBs. We favor a magnetized neutron star accreting from an intermediate mass donor at a persistently high rate with the flares arising from instabilities at the disk-magnetosphere boundary. If confirmed, M81F4 might represent a hidden population of XRBs in which sustained, magnetically-regulated accretion can lead to brief episodes of super-Eddington emission.
item.dc:creator: Jiachang Zhang, Zhiyuan Li, Xiangdong Li, Tong Bao, Ziqian Hua, ShanShan Weng

item.title: A blazar is a blazar is a blazar ... Comparing long-term varaibility properties of PKS 1510-089 and PKS 2155-304
item.description: arXiv:2610.23359v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blazars are typically divided by spectral appearance; may that be strength of optical emission lines or the frequency of the synchrotron peak. However, this may say nothing about the variability properties of the various types. Here, we study the long-term variability properties with nearly 20 years of multiwavelength data of one flat-spectrum radio quasar, PKS 1510-089, and one high-frequency-peaked BL Lac object, PKS 2155-304. Both exhibit strong variability with an energy-dependent variability amplitude. Using the total data sets, we do not find any correlation between the various bands. While the flux distributions of PKS 2155-304 are compatible with log-normal functions, this is not the case for PKS 1510-089. We conclude that the one-zone model is inadequate to describe the long-term evolution of blazars, requiring multi-zone or stratified models. Nevertheless, the underlying jet physics appear similar between the two types and in both sources the variability is, in fact, variable.
item.dc:creator: M. Zacharias, A. Wierzcholska

item.title: Three-dimensional spatial modelling of nuclear de-excitation lines
item.description: arXiv:2610.23380v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Galactic cosmic rays (GCRs) are thought to originate from shock acceleration in supernova remnants, but interstellar ionization rates suggest an additional low-energy cosmic-ray (LECR) component. LECRs excite nuclei in the ISM, producing MeV gamma-ray line emission through subsequent de-excitation. Observations of this emission can constrain the LECR flux, morphology, and acceleration mechanisms. We construct all-sky maps of Galactic de-excitation emission using three-dimensional (3D) CR distribution models. By comparing them with the Galactic diffuse gamma-ray emission, we assess the detectability of the de-excitation line components against the underlying continuum. We calculate the emission by combining 3D CR distributions from GALPROP and gamma-ray production cross sections from TALYS. We also model an additional LECR component motivated by the high ionization rates measured in the ISM. The predicted de-excitation emission is relatively weak when integrated over the broad regions commonly adopted in MeV gamma-ray analyses ($|l|\leq30^{\circ}$ and $|b|\leq15^{\circ}$), contributing only $\lesssim 1\%$ above the leptonic continuum even considering the additional LECR component. The all-sky maps reveal that, in the standard scenario, the de-excitation-to-leptonic flux ratio remains low over the entire sky, reaching at most ${\sim}20\%$ toward the Galactic anticenter. In contrast, models including an additional LECR component exhibit a pronounced enhancement toward the GC, where the ratio exceeds $100\%$, indicating favourable prospects for detection through spatially resolved analyses. The 6.1-to-4.4 MeV intensity ratio is particularly sensitive to the maximum energy of the injected LECR spectrum, varying by up to ${\sim} 30\%$. Future MeV gamma-ray observatories could thus identify a distinct LECR population and constrain its acceleration and transport.
item.dc:creator: Tomohiko Oka, Thomas Siegert, Tristan Bouchet, Laura Eisenberger, Mika A. Gelowicz, Saurabh Mittal, Rudi Reinhardt, Manuel R. H. W. Skalka, Dimitris Tsatsis, Hiroki Yoneda, Manja Zimmerer

item.title: Prospects for Simultaneously Detecting Long and Short Duration Gravitational Waves from Pulsar Glitches with Current and Future Detectors
item.description: arXiv:2610.23385v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The internal mechanisms that drive the sudden change in rotation frequency in pulsar glitches could emit gravitational waves (GWs) at multiple time scales. The potential for GW analyses to detect both long and short forms of emission ("tCW-like" and "burst-like") improves as the detectors increase in sensitivity. We aim to examine how future detectors fare in making this joint measurement. By examining past glitches from the ATNF catalog, we quantify the double-detectability prospects of current- and next-generation GW detector networks. We further explore what astrophysical constraints could be placed following a double non-detection using extrapolations from the 2024 Vela pulsar glitch as a stand-in example. We find that a network with at least one next-generation detector greatly increases the probability of double-detection for many known glitching pulsars and improves the detection threshold in glitch energy by nearly two orders of magnitude over existing LIGO detectors. Additionally, double non-detections with networks with at least one next-generation detector could place dramatically improved limits on properties of the pulsar.
item.dc:creator: M. Ball, D. Keitel

item.title: Exploring Cosmic Rays from Gravity-Limited Acceleration at Supermassive Black Holes
item.description: arXiv:2610.23393v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We show that horizon-scale magnetic fields around supermassive black holes (SMBHs), only limited by gravity, yield a universal, model-independent ceiling on electromagnetic energy density. For rotating SMBHs, this field enables particle acceleration up to $\sim\!10^{27}$\,eV set solely by fundamental constants. We identify a parameter space in accretion rate and magnetic field strength in which quiescent nuclei simultaneously satisfy the transparency conditions for Ultra-High-Energy Cosmic Rays (UHECR) escape and the field requirements for reaching Ultra-High Energies (UHE), naturally complementing photon-rich Active Galactic Nuclei (AGN), which favor neutrino production but suppress UHECR escape. We observe that, when including curvature energy losses, the energy of the primaries scales weakly as $E_{\rm curv}\!\propto\!M^{1/4}$ and allows to achieve UHE across different compositions and SMBHs masses ($10^6$--$10^{10}\,M_\odot$), without requiring extreme spins or super-Eddington accretion. A cross-correlation of the Pierre Auger Observatory (PAO) public data with galaxies hosting reliably measured SMBH masses, separating AGN from quiescent hosts, reveals marginal local excesses ($\lesssim\!2.8\sigma$) consistent with isotropy after correcting for the look-elsewhere effect. The framework provides a direct link between black-hole physics and the maximum energies of cosmic particles, and defines concrete observational tests for next-generation UHECR datasets.
item.dc:creator: Elena Manao, Elisa Resconi, Frank M. Rieger, Paolo Padovani, Gia Dvali

item.title: Impact of neutron captures on the r-process: I. Propagation of statistical model uncertainties
item.description: arXiv:2610.23395v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Background: The r-process is responsible for producing about half of the elements heavier than iron in the Universe, but the underlying nuclear physics is still largely inaccessible to experiments and relies on theoretical calculations. Purpose: We aim to quantify the impact of statistical model uncertainties on the r-process with a large set of neutron-capture rates within the Hauser-Feshbach framework with varied statistical model parameters. Propagating neutron-capture rates to r-process calculations of various astrophysical sites allows us to link abundance features to nuclear uncertainties. Methods: We calculate neutron-capture reactivities using different nuclear level density (NLD) and gamma-ray strength function (GSF) prescriptions. We study their impact on r-process calculations for individual trajectories, mass-integrated ejecta from a neutron-star-merger, and a broad set of 10,000 parametric trajectories with a wide range of electron fractions and entropies. Results: The final abundances are more sensitive to NLDs than to GSFs. Selected NLDs produce pronounced abundance changes between the lanthanides and the third peak. Although the variation is reduced in the mass-integrated total ejecta, a subpeak at A=172-178 and systematic abundance changes at A=180-194 persist. The parametric trajectories show that the NLD sensitivity is greater in the cold r-process regime, where neutron captures continue after photodissociations have become ineffective. Additional conditions with large NLD sensitivities are found at intermediate electron fractions, where small changes in the matter flow can lead to significant differences in the final abundances. Conclusions: Systematic differences in neutron-capture rates between NLD prescriptions affect the final r-process abundances. Therefore, improved experimental constraints and theoretical descriptions of NLDs in these regions are needed.
item.dc:creator: Yu An, Jan Kuske, Almudena Arcones

item.title: SN 2025wiu: A Type Ib Supernova with Post-Peak Optical Rebrightening
item.description: arXiv:2610.23414v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We present optical photometric and optical/near-infrared spectroscopic observations of SN 2025wiu, a Type Ib supernova (SN) at z = 0.046927. The r-band light curve exhibits an initial maximum of approximately -18.2 mag, followed by a weaker optical rebrightening reaching approximately -17.8 mag at +38 days in the rest frame relative to the first maximum. However, the reconstructed bolometric light curve does not show a distinct second peak, but instead exhibits a reduced decline rate during the corresponding phase. The spectra consistently show Type Ib features without narrow emission components associated with circumstellar material. The late-time bolometric decline rate of 0.054 +/- 0.008 mag/day is faster than expected for complete trapping of 56Co decay. A radioactive-decay model for the first peak requires nickel mass = 0.47 solar masses, above the range typical of SNe Ib. A combined radioactive-decay and circumstellar-interaction model reproduces the full bolometric light curve with nickel mass ~ 0.38 solar masses, ejecta mass ~ 4.7 solar masses, and an effective circumstellar mass of ~ 0.10 solar masses, with the interaction contributing from the first peak onward. The lack of interaction signatures in the spectra favours an aspherical, disk-like circumstellar structure engulfed by the ejecta, in which the interaction energy is thermalized below the ejecta photosphere; the fitted circumstellar parameters are therefore effective values rather than direct measurements of the circumstellar geometry. SN 2025wiu demonstrates that optical rebrightening does not necessarily imply a genuine bolometric secondary maximum and highlights the importance of multi-band observations for identifying the powering mechanisms of double-peaked stripped-envelope supernovae.
item.dc:creator: Cheng-Han Lai, Ting-Wan Chen, Yu-Hao Zhang, Liang-Duan Liu, Jesper Sollerman, Amar Aryan, Anirban Dutta, Sheng Yang, Christoffer Fremling, Matthew J. Graham, David Hale, K. -Ryan Hinds, Mansi M. Kasliwal, Frank J. Masci, Reed L. Riddle, Sam Rose, Ben Rusholme, Niharika Sravan

item.title: ExHaLe-jet: Modeling blazar jets with an extended hadro-leptonic radiation code
item.description: arXiv:2610.23425v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Blazars - active galaxies with the jet pointing at Earth - emit across all electromagnetic wavelengths. As the one-zone model becomes increasingly inadequate to describe blazar emission, more elaborate models are needed. In order to self-consistently describe the entire electromagnetic spectrum, extended jet models are necessary. Notably, kinetic descriptions of extended jets can provide the temporal and spatial evolution of the particle species and the full electromagnetic output. ExHaLe-jet is a lepto-hadronic, extended-jet code allowing for in-depth studies of the particle and radiation evolution on all scales. Here, we present our ongoing study regarding acceleration scenarios of particles within the large-scale jet structure. A single acceleration of particles at the jet base (or elsewhere) is insufficient to produce sufficient photon flux. Thus, re-acceleration through, e.g., consecutive shocks along the jet is needed. We explore two possible scenarios for this.
item.dc:creator: M. Zacharias, A. Zech, A. Reimer, C. Boisson

item.title: Foreground dependence of the 20 GeV Galactic halo gamma-ray excess and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN event
item.description: arXiv:2610.23713v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We assess the dark matter interpretation of the 20 GeV gamma-ray halo excess reported by Totani and its proposed connection to the LUX-ZEPLIN (LZ) high-energy nuclear-recoil event, which independently favors dark matter masses above about 200 GeV. Using fifteen years of Fermi-LAT data, we reproduce the excess under the original assumptions and test it against 281 Galactic diffuse emission configurations, three descriptions of the Fermi bubbles, four of Loop I, and uniform and X-ray-brightness-weighted eROSITA bubbles templates. A component correlated with a Navarro-Frenk-White (NFW) annihilation template remains with finer spatial binning and the instrumental response included. Outside the Fermi bubbles footprint, it is detected at nominal significances of about 4-16$\sigma$ over 5.6-130 GeV, falling to 1-7$\sigma$ when the enlarged boundaries of a recent substructured bubbles model are also excluded. With the substructured model, which improves the fit substantially, the component remains at 7-18$\sigma$ in four of six representative foreground configurations. However, its amplitude and spectrum depend strongly on the foreground model, and no tested foreground yields a single NFW normalization across the sky, including with additional spatial freedom in the eROSITA bubbles. Simulations show that foreground mismodeling can produce spurious NFW-correlated emission of the observed amplitude, and that residual-derived bubbles templates can bias the recovered spectrum. The 420 GeV $W^+W^-$ spectrum motivated by the LZ connection describes the data for some foreground models but is disfavored by others. These results disfavor interpreting the full excess as annihilation in a smooth NFW halo and weaken the case for a common origin with the LZ event, but they do not exclude a dark matter contribution to the persistent halo-like residual. [abridged]
item.dc:creator: Kevork N. Abazajian, Youyou Li, Oscar Macias

item.title: Beyond Mergers: the Role of Metallicity in Forming a Reservoir of Massive and Detached Binary Black Hole Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.20736v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Isolated binary evolution is a key pathway to forming binary black hole (BBH) mergers. However, the observed gravitational-wave population indicates it may not account for all mergers, especially those with high primary black hole mass ($\gtrsim 30 M_{\odot}$). Using the binary population synthesis code \texttt{POSYDON}, we simulate populations of binary systems at eight metallicities from $10^{-4}$ to $2\,Z_\odot$ and classify each BH-forming binary as a merging BBH, a detached BBH, or a system disrupted during BH formation. We find that metallicity shapes these populations differently, especially for high BH masses ($\gtrsim 25 M_{\odot}$). At lower metallicities, between $10^{-2}$ and $0.45\,Z_\odot$, massive BHs continue to form but become increasingly unlikely to merge: the number of massive merging BBHs declines sharply, while the detached population remains abundant. For $25$--$35\,M_\odot$ BHs, the detached-to-merging ratio increases by more than two orders of magnitude across this metallicity range. After weighting by cosmic star formation, massive BHs are found predominantly in detached binaries with orbital periods $\gtrsim 10^2$ days. Therefore, isolated binary evolution can form massive BBHs even if it rarely produces massive BBH mergers, leaving behind a massive and detached population that may be driven to merger through dynamical interactions in dense stellar environments.
item.dc:creator: Siyuan Chen, Monica Gallegos-Garcia

item.title: Modeling extreme mass-ratio inspirals in astrophysical and dark-matter environments
item.description: arXiv:2610.22480v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Extreme mass-ratio inspirals offer a powerful probe of massive black holes and their environments, but interpreting their signals requires accurate models of orbital dynamics and radiation. Here we bring together advances in black-hole perturbation theory to establish a unified relativistic framework for adiabatic inspirals in perturbative astrophysical environments. Built on the modified Teukolsky formalism, the framework requires neither post-Newtonian nor slow-rotation approximations. As a first application, we calculate the leading cloud-induced corrections to gravitational-wave fluxes and conservative orbital dynamics for circular, equatorial inspirals around a rotating black hole surrounded by a synchronized ultralight scalar cloud, combining these corrections with the previously calculated scalar response. In our fiducial system, a cloud containing $10^{-4}$ of the black-hole mass produces about $-57.3$ radians of orbital dephasing over two years. The phase contributions from gravitational-wave flux corrections and background-induced orbital shifts each exceed the scalar contribution in magnitude and partially cancel, highlighting the need for coupled matter-gravity modeling. Extensible to other environments and modified gravity theories, our framework provides the relativistic inputs needed to assess detection losses and parameter biases, and to probe the nature of black-hole environments with future space-based gravitational-wave observations.
item.dc:creator: Dongjun Li, Hao-Jui Kuan, Colin Weller, Chaoyi Yang, Kelvin Ka-Ho Lam, Patrick Bourg, Adrian Ka-Wai Chung, Yanbei Chen, Nicol\'as Yunes, Huan Yang

item.title: Four Which I Knew Not: The Hexadecapole Nearly Cancels the Octupole in Librating Kozai-Lidov Cycles
item.description: arXiv:2610.22487v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Phenomena requiring close proximity between two bodies, from black-hole mergers to hot Jupiters, may originate in hierarchical triples, in which secular torques from a distant companion drive the inner binary's eccentricity nearly to unity. Population syntheses of these channels commonly integrate the double-averaged (DA) secular equations truncated at octupole order. We show that, for a fixed outer orbit, this truncation fails for the slow evolution on librating Kozai-Lidov cycles, in which the argument of pericenter librates. On these cycles the leading octupole kicks to $j_z$, the component of the inner angular momentum along the outer one, cancel pairwise, and the hexadecapole enters at the order of the surviving octupole torque, with the opposite sign. Strikingly, as the inner mass ratio vanishes the two nearly cancel, and their sum changes sign within the librating window, so octupole-truncated integrations omit part of the leading slow torque on this class. For $|j_z|\ll1$, the slow dynamics driven by the hexadecapole is approximately solved analytically as a simple pendulum in the doubled azimuth of the eccentricity vector, with closed-form coefficients on rotating and librating cycles. For a circular outer orbit the hexadecapole-modified cycles are solved exactly. For unequal inner masses the octupole adds to the pendulum's torque on librating cycles, where its alternating kick can also flip orbits, and generally dominates rotating ones. DA integrations follow the predicted excursions, periods and flip criteria. Population consequences depend on the validity of the high-eccentricity reduction and on other processes affecting the cycles.
item.dc:creator: Ygal Y. Klein

item.title: Constraints on Decaying Dark Matter with $B=1$ from Fermi-LAT
item.description: arXiv:2610.22530v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We investigate the gamma ray signatures of fermionic dark matter that carries one unit of baryon number and decays into three quarks. We compute the expected prompt and secondary gamma-ray spectra for a representative range of final state flavor combinations. By comparing these spectra to Fermi-LAT measurements of the isotropic gamma-ray background, we derive exclusion limits on the lifetime. We observe that depending on the dark matter mass and the flavor of the final state, the lifetime bounds on decays of $B=1$ dark matter can differ by up to a factor of two from those on decays of $B=0$ dark matter. Furthermore, light-quark final states generally yield stronger bounds at lower masses, whereas heavy-quark final states can yield comparable or stronger bounds at masses of tens of TeV and above.
item.dc:creator: Can Kilic, Zhi-Xiang Yang, Taewook Youn

item.title: The transformative power of ALMA2040 for mm-VLBI
item.description: arXiv:2610.22662v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The Event Horizon Telescope (EHT) has resolved horizon-scale emission in M87* and Sgr A*. Extending these observations to fainter black holes, multiple frequencies, and evolving structures requires greater sensitivity and new observing capabilities. We investigate how ALMA2040 could expand the scientific reach of global millimeter very long baseline interferometry (mm-VLBI), compared with ALMA's Wideband Sensitivity Upgrade (WSU). Phasing a larger ALMA array and enabling simultaneous observations across multiple ALMA bands would improve sensitivity and frequency phase transfer, providing spectral and polarimetric diagnostics of gravity, accretion flows, magnetic fields, and relativistic jets. In the configurations studied, ALMA2040 achieves sub-mJy baseline sensitivity at 230 GHz and improves prospects for faint-source imaging at 345 GHz, opening a path from individual horizon-scale targets toward population studies. Simulated observations of M87* show improved multi-frequency recovery of emission from the compact ring-like region toward the jet base, enabling studies of the accretion-jet connection. For Sgr A*, simulations of interstellar scattering mitigation yield a 27% reduction in the error of the recovered intrinsic source structure relative to the WSU configuration. Beyond black holes, these capabilities benefit geometric-distance measurements, stellar masers, compact transients, and other applications of high-resolution astrophysics. Together with rapid-response capabilities across the VLBI network, ALMA2040 could support a transition from isolated snapshots toward multi-frequency, time-resolved studies of compact sources.
item.dc:creator: The Event Horizon Telescope Collaboration

item.title: A New AI/ML Based Image Reconstruction Technique for Hard X-ray Coded Aperture Imagers
item.description: arXiv:2610.22709v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Here we demonstrate a new AI/ML based image reconstruction method for coded-aperture instruments that provides a pathway for embedded real-time use on-board spaceflight missions. Using the Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) for our initial simulated demonstration, we used our new technique to replace the standard Fast Fourier Transform (FFT) based image reconstruction pipeline. In our alternative approach, we have created a neural network that maps detector counts directly to source positions using simulated responses from selected Swift Burst Alert Telescope (BAT) observations. The network combines convolutional feature extraction with attention and is trained at around 900 source counts. Under zero background noise, it achieves over 93\% exact-pixel localization accuracy with 400 detected source photons. The model maintains at least 90\% exact-pixel localization accuracy with up to 8{,}500 added background counts for sources with 900 detected photons. Within the evaluated region of BAT's field of view, these results show that source position can be recovered from sparse coded-aperture measurements in a wide-field instrument. A key feature of this technique is that explicit inclusion of the mask pattern is not required. This allows us to train the algorithm to "see" using data accumulated from an imaging system. These new non-traditional imaging techniques show substantial promise in enabling efficient imaging using non-planar geometries, which will enable new classes of hard X/$\gamma$-ray imaging systems and simultaneously improve imaging capability for currently operating instruments.
item.dc:creator: Shayla Sharmin, Branden Allen

item.title: A Multiwavelength View of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5: an X-ray Luminous and Eclipsing Dwarf Nova
item.description: arXiv:2610.22790v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We report the independent discovery of the cataclysmic variable (CV) SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 using Southern Photometric Local Universe Survey 12 band photometry, following its initial identification via ASAS-SN variability. Here, we investigate the system using optical photometry alongside optical and X-ray spectroscopy. High-cadence optical light curves from publicly available TESS data and a dedicated campaign at the Pico dos Dias Observatory in Brazil revealed a highly inclined system exhibiting pronounced eclipses with an orbital period of 1.81 hours. We found no evidence of a WD spin period. Despite seasonal gaps, the long-term ASAS-SN light curve revealed several outbursts (15 with $\Delta$mag $\sim$ 1.5 brighter than the mean magnitude) and one superoutburst over the past decade. During Swift X-ray telescope observations, the system exhibited X-ray luminosity of $8.5 \times 10^{31}$ erg s$^{-1}$ in the 0.3-10\,keV band, originating from thermal plasma emission at a temperature consistent with accretion shocks. Optical spectroscopy from the Gemini Multi-Object Spectrographs on the Gemini South telescope confirms the CV nature of the system, showing strong, double-peaked H and HeI emission lines alongside a weak HeII4686 line. Altogether, these features strongly support the classification of SPLUS J102139.31-282247.5 as a quiescent, eclipsing dwarf nova with an unusually high X-ray luminosity.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Silva de Araujo, Raimundo Lopes de Oliveira, Koji Mukai, Raymundo Baptista, Albert Bruch, Romualdo Eleuterio, Angela Krabbe, Claudia Mendes de Oliveira

item.title: $\texttt{GASTRO-BH}$: Effects of a Central Black Hole in GSE-like Dwarf-galaxy Mergers Around Milky Way-like Hosts
item.description: arXiv:2610.22860v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent evidence points to an intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) in the most massive globular cluster of the Milky Way, $\omega$ Centauri. This globular cluster is commonly associated with the Gaia-Sausage/Enceladus (GSE) dwarf galaxy, the last major merger event of our Galaxy, as its nuclear star cluster remnant. Motivated by this, we investigate whether the interaction between a bright GSE-like dwarf galaxy with stellar mass in the range $10^{8.5}$--$10^{9.7}$ solar masses and a Milky Way-like host can either suppress or enhance the growth of a central black hole (BH) during the merger process. To this end, we perform high-resolution $N$-body and smoothed particle hydrodynamics (SPH) simulations with the ChaNGa framework and a modified, angular-momentum-aware Bondi-Hoyle accretion prescription, considering both isolated dwarf galaxies and merger simulations with different stellar feedback efficiencies. The merger simulations show that the interaction does not halt BH accretion; instead, tidal interactions and gas inflows during pericentric passages strongly enhance accretion, leading to BH mass growth by more than two orders of magnitude in both low- and high-feedback models. The enhanced accretion is accompanied by suppressed star formation in the dwarf galaxy. Our results suggest that mergers similar to the GSE event can efficiently fuel IMBH growth in satellite galaxies rather than suppress it. This may be in tension with the estimated low mass of the proposed IMBH in $\omega$ Centauri, but it could provide a mechanism for triggering active galactic nucleus activity in dwarf galaxies.
item.dc:creator: Pedro Naethe Motta, Jo\~ao A. S. Amarante, Guilherme Limberg, Lais Borbolato, Chervin F. P. Laporte, Zhao-Yu Li, Reinaldo Santos-Lima, Victor P. Debattista, Marcelo C. Vicentin

item.title: Seeing Through the RFI Mask: DT-FISTA Inpainting of Pulsar Dynamic Spectra via Fourier Sparsity
item.description: arXiv:2610.23140v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Radio frequency interference (RFI) frequently contaminates radio observations, and excising affected samples leaves masked regions in sampled images. Replacing masked samples with zero or the mean causes spectral leakage in Fourier-domain power representations. This contamination is particularly severe for modern pulsar scintillation studies, which rely on identifying and characterizing faint parabolic scintillation arcs in secondary spectra, the 2D power spectra of dynamic spectra. Scintillation arcs probe discrete scattering screens in the interstellar medium (ISM) and constrain their physical properties. However, leakage can obscure faint arcs whose power is often $<10^{-3}$ of the dominant pulsar signal power. Wiener inpainting can mitigate this leakage, but a dense implementation requires $\mathcal{O}(N^2)$ memory and $\mathcal{O}(JN^2)$ time for $N$ pixels and $J$ iterations, which is computationally expensive for full-resolution spectra containing millions of pixels. We introduce the decreasing-threshold fast iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (DT-FISTA). Using a sparse Fourier representation, DT-FISTA initially estimates masked intensities from the strongest Fourier components and progressively refines them with weaker components as the soft threshold decreases. Nesterov momentum extrapolation accelerates these updates. Each iteration uses 2D fast Fourier transforms (FFT) and pointwise operations, requiring $\mathcal{O}(N\log N)$ time and $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory. Tests on $300\times300$ pixel patches from Five-hundred-meter Aperture Spherical radio Telescope (FAST) observations yield lower reconstruction errors than the dense Wiener implementation, with runtime and memory requirements reduced by factors $>10^3$. Applied to full-resolution dynamic spectra, DT-FISTA suppresses mask-induced artifacts and reveals previously obscured faint arcs, enabling efficient ISM studies.
item.dc:creator: Yuanshang Huang, Xun Shi

item.title: Andreev Beta Conversion and Bulk Viscosity in Superfluid Neutron-Star Matter
item.description: arXiv:2610.23581v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Bulk viscosity in neutron-star matter is attributed to the phase lag between a density oscillation and weak beta equilibration. We point out a distinct coherent channel when the baryonic component that stores the condensate is superfluid: an effective beta-conversion event between a neutron condensate and normal protons can proceed as an Andreev process, converting a particle-like excitation into a hole-like excitation while adding or removing a Cooper pair from the condensate. The resulting Andreev contribution to beta equilibration is fourth order in the effective conversion vertex, is enhanced by anomalous neutron Green's functions, and is not captured by standard Urca process. We identify the density, temperature, and oscillation-frequency regimes where this channel can dominate viscous damping of neutron-star oscillations and mergers.
item.dc:creator: Tingyu Zhang, Honoka Hoshino, Hiroyuki Tajima, Motoi Tachibana, Mariusz Sadzikowski

item.title: Clustering of JWST LRDs. Implications for PBHs and other early-forming seeds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23806v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use the observed abundance and spatial clustering of JWST little red dots (LRDs) over z = 4--8 to confront two formation scenarios: the standard picture in which LRDs form in virialized dark-matter halos, and one in which they are seeded by a dynamically subdominant population of primordial black holes (PBHs). The halo formation scenario accounts for both observables naturally and without fine-tuning. In the PBH scenario, matching the observed LRD abundance requires a negligibly small PBH mass fraction, and a power-spectrum analysis shows that such a Poisson isocurvature component predicts a clustering signal far below what is observed. The same conclusion holds for any population of dynamically subdominant early-forming seeds, unless their initial clustering is finely tuned or their activity is tied to massive host halos. We conclude that the spatial clustering of JWST LRDs strongly favours the standard halo formation picture and disfavours PBHs, or similar early-forming seeds, as a randomly activated LRD population; PBHs remain viable as seeds only if their activity is governed by massive host halos, in which case clustering alone cannot distinguish them from astrophysical seeds.
item.dc:creator: Gert H\"utsi

item.title: Hydrodynamic instabilities in long-term three-dimensional simulations of neutrino-driven supernovae of 13 red supergiant progenitors
item.description: arXiv:2511.11796v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We present long-term three-dimensional (3D) simulations of Type-IIP supernovae (SNe) for 13 non-rotating, single-star, red-supergiant (RSG) progenitors with zero-age-main-sequence masses between 12.5 M$_{\odot}$ and 27.3 M$_{\odot}$. The explosions were modelled with a parametric treatment of neutrino heating to obtain defined energies, ${}^{56}$Ni yields, and neutron-star properties in agreement with previous results. Our 3D SN models were evolved from core bounce until 10 days to study how the large-scale mixing of chemical elements depends on the progenitor structure. Rayleigh-Taylor instabilities (RTIs), which grow at the (C+O)/He and He/H interfaces and interact with the reverse shock forming after the SN shock has passed the He/H interface, play a crucial role in the outward mixing of ${}^{56}$Ni into the hydrogen envelope. We find most extreme ${}^{56}$Ni mixing and the highest maximum ${}^{56}$Ni velocities in lower-mass (LM) explosions despite lower explosion energies, and the weakest ${}^{56}$Ni mixing in the 3D explosions of the most massive RSGs. The efficiency of radial ${}^{56}$Ni mixing anti-correlates linearly with the helium-core mass and correlates positively with the magnitude of a local maximum of $\rho r^3$ in the helium shell. This maximum causes shock deceleration and therefore facilitates high growth factors of RTI at the (C+O)/He interface in the LM explosions. Therefore fast-moving ${}^{56}$Ni created by the asymmetric neutrino-heating mechanism is carried into the ubiquitous RT-unstable region near the He/H interface and ultimately far into the envelopes of the exploding RSGs. Our correlations may aid improving mixing prescriptions in 1D SN models and deducing progenitor structures from observed SN properties..
item.dc:creator: Beatrice Giudici (Universitat de Val\`encia), Michael Gabler (Universitat de Val\`encia), Hans-Thomas Janka (Max Planck Institute for Astrophysics, Garching)

item.title: Charged-current neutrino opacity within the relativistic Hartree-Fock framework for astrophysical simulations of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers
item.description: arXiv:2605.17563v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Neutrinos and their weak interactions play a vital role in the physics of core-collapse supernovae and binary neutron star mergers. Their description within astrophysical simulations, including the weak rates, is of pivotal importance not only for the prediction of accurate neutrino fluxes and spectra, including the associated conditions relevant to nucleosynthesis, neutrinos are also responsible for heating and cooling of the stellar plasma as well as the transport of lepton number and entropy. In the present article, we develop an essential improvement of the description of the underlying nuclear medium, necessary for the calculations of charged-current weak rates, with the inclusion of explicitly momentum-dependent nuclear interactions. To this end, we introduce the relativistic Hartree-Fock (RHF) approach and the associated momentum-dependent nucleon self-energies. We discuss the resulting neutrino and antineutrino opacities and find large discrepancies comparing the weak rates at the RHF level with those of commonly used relativistic mean-field (RMF) models. In particular, we observe a substantial shift of previously reported large medium-dependent modifications associated with the RMF approach.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: K. Soko{\l}owski, A. Kumar and T. Fischer, Phys. Rev. D 114, 083012 (2026)
item.dc:creator: Kamil Soko{\l}owski, Anil Kumar, Tobias Fischer

item.title: Can current models predict the local black hole merger rate?
item.description: arXiv:2606.02725v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: After four observational runs, the Ligo-Virgo-Kagra collaboration estimated a local binary black hole (BBH) merger rate density of $R_{0,\textrm{LVK}}\simeq 14-26\,\textrm{Gpc}^{-3}\,\textrm{yr}^{-1}$ within the 90% credible interval. Some previous studies already pointed out that, when a realistic evolution of the metallicity-dependent cosmic star formation rate density (SFRD) is adopted, theoretical models predict a local BBH merger rate density that exceeds the observed value by at least a factor of $\sim 10$. In this paper, we confirm and strengthen this claim by constructing an empirical model for the SFRD and metallicity evolution that includes a correction accounting for iron abundance. The adopted metallicity relation is flexible, enabling us to bracket the wide range of observational uncertainties. We show that, even under the most conservative assumptions regarding both the SFRD and the metallicity relation, the local BBH merger rate density is overestimated by a factor $> 10$. Attempts to reconcile the predicted and observed merger rates by modifying only the metallicity-dependent SFRD would require unrealistically high metallicities ($Z>Z_\odot$) even in low-mass galaxies at high redshift. This finding indicates that revisions to the treatment of stellar and binary evolution are necessary to achieve consistency between theoretical predictions and observations. We suggest that even a modest steepening of the delay-time distribution could help alleviate this tension.
item.dc:creator: Lumen Boco, Michele Bosi, Cecilia Sgalletta, Amedeo Romagnolo, Michela Mapelli

item.title: Transition from Diffusion to Drift-Dominated Cosmic Ray Transport and the Origin of the Knee
item.description: arXiv:2606.28141v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In a magnetic field with a complex topology, as can be the Galactic magnetic field, cosmic ray transport cannot simply be described by diffusion parallel and perpendicular to magnetic field lines, because the gradients and curvature of the large-scale magnetic field induce drift motions. These effects become especially important at high energies. Here we revisit the possibility that the competition between diffusion and drifts may lead to a knee in the cosmic ray spectrum. We carry out test-particle simulations of cosmic ray transport in a mock Galactic magnetic field made of a regular large scale component, with a non-trivial topology and a homogeneous and isotropic turbulent magnetic field, with a spectrum that is assumed to be Kolmogorov-like in the basic setup. These simulations are used to infer the escape time and the grammage accumulated by cosmic rays with energy in the TeV--10 PeV energy range. In the case of a large scale magnetic field with a purely azimuthal structure, the drift due to the curvature of magnetic field lines produces a knee in the PeV range, but the model fails to reproduce the grammage, due to the exceedingly low value of the perpendicular diffusion coefficient. If the large scale magnetic field acquires a component perpendicular to the Galactic disc, the parallel diffusion coefficient becomes quickly dominant in terms of particle escape, and drifts are unable to compete. A knee structure does not appear in such a scenario. However, if the parallel diffusion coefficient becomes energy independent at $E\gtrsim 1$ TeV, a knee may arise around PeV energies due to drift dominance. We discuss two cases in which this situation may occur.
item.dc:creator: Luis Enrique Espinosa Castro, Carmelo Evoli, Pasquale Blasi

item.title: Gas Motions in Hydra-A: XRISM Constraints on ICM Kinematics Across Jet-Inflated Cavities
item.description: arXiv:2607.18315v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report on two deep XRISM observations of the central and northern regions of Hydra-A's X-ray atmosphere, covering the bubbles inflated by jets from the central galaxy's active galactic nucleus. We use spatial-spectral mixing, combining Chandra's high spatial resolution with XRISM's high spectral resolution, to investigate atmospheric kinematics. The velocity dispersion in the northern region, $\sigma_v = 140^{+30}_{-20}$ km s$^{-1}$, is comparable to that in the central region ($\sigma_v = 162 \pm 10$ km s$^{-1}$). We show that motion of the large-scale cocoon shock front could be responsible for the large dispersion toward the north. The dispersion in the northeast quarter of the central pointing, $\sigma_v = 260 \pm 50$ km s$^{-1}$, is among the highest measured. This region contains an X-ray-bright feature previously identified as metal-rich, possibly gas uplifted in the wake of previous-generation cavities. Dispersions in all other quarter regions are low ($\sigma_v \leq 180$ km s$^{-1}$) and consistent with previous XRISM results from other objects. The kinetic energy at the center is comparable to the enthalpies of the cavities, while in the north it is roughly an order of magnitude smaller. The jet thus drives gas motion efficiently at smaller scales ($r < 95$ kpc) and inefficiently at larger scales ($95-317$ kpc toward the north along the jet). A bulk flow toward our line of sight of $-100 \pm 30$ km s$^{-1}$ in the southwest quarter of the central pointing, measured with respect to the central galaxy, is also observed, possibly due to sloshing. No significant bulk motion was detected in any other region.
item.dc:creator: Anwesh Majumder, B. R. McNamara, P. E. J. Nulsen, H. Russell, T. Rose, T. Heckman, A. Simionescu, A. Fabian, M. W. Wise, N. Werner, M. McDonald

item.title: An "inside-out" approach to modeling supermassive black hole binary inspiral
item.description: arXiv:2608.06269v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The inspiral and merger of two supermassive black holes (SMBHs) releases immense energy in low-frequency gravitational waves (GWs). Recent pulsar timing array (PTA) observations of the stochastic nHz GW background (GWB) are consistent with a SMBH binary origin. GW data from PTAs and from the upcoming Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) can probe late-stage binary evolution where electromagnetic constraints are scarce. However, the complexity of the relevant astrophysics necessitates a well optimized approach. I argue that a key physical quantity to constrain with PTAs is the orbital semi-major axis at which binary inspiral transitions from the astrophysical to the GW-dominated regime ($a_{\rm GW}$). This quantity should be treated as a free parameter in analysis of the GWB. Using this premise, I present a simple analytic framework for modeling SMBH binary inspiral in an "inside-out" fashion. At orbital separations slightly larger than $a_{\rm GW}$, a power-law scaling for the astrophysical inspiral timescale is assumed, while the outermost phase (prior to the PTA regime) is simply modeled via a delay time. I show that the GWB spectral shape and amplitude are most sensitive to $a_{\rm GW}$ (normalized to $10^9 M_{\odot}$, equal-mass binaries and expressed in gravitational units), with weaker dependence on the inner power-law index and the outer delay time. The GWB is largely insensitive to the mass and mass-ratio scaling of $a_{\rm GW}$ and to the boundary between the inner and outer astrophysical inspiral regimes. I compare with models for gas- and stellar-driven binary inspiral and discuss implications for LISA and for GW source parameter inference.
item.dc:creator: Laura Blecha

item.title: IXPE observation of the new magnetar source EP J223759.5+531421
item.description: arXiv:2609.25958v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report on the detection of polarized X-ray emission from the new Galactic magnetar EP J223759.5+531421, discovered by the Einstein Probe Wide-field X-ray Telescope on 2026 June 28. The Imaging X-ray Polarimetry Explorer (IXPE) follow-up observation started on 2026 July 6 and detected the source at a (absorbed) flux of $\approx 4.5\times 10^{-11} \, \mathrm{ erg\,cm^2\,s}^{-1}$ ($2$--$7.5\, \mathrm{keV}$ range), confirming the presence of two thermally emitting regions on the star surface, with temperatures $\approx 0.5$ and $\approx 1\, \mathrm{keV}$. A significant (at $> 4\sigma$ confidence level) phase- and energy-integrated polarization degree of $\approx 7\%$ was detected with the polarization angle $\approx -2^\circ$ East of the celestial North. The two thermal components exhibit quite different polarization properties, with the hotter one being more polarized. The difference is larger in the phase-folded data, with the polarization degree reaching $\sim 63\%$ in the range $4$--$7.5\,\mathrm{keV}$, in correspondence with the secondary peak of the pulse profile, and never exceeding $\sim 30\%$ at lower energies. The polarization angle continuously oscillates from $-90^\circ$ to $+90^\circ$ over one rotational cycle and is well fit by the rotating vector model, with an inclination of the line of sight and of the magnetic dipole axis relative to the star spin axis of $\approx 28^\circ$ and $\approx 109^\circ$, respectively. The data point to an emission geometry in which the cold thermal component likely originates from two antipodal caps, possibly in a magnetically condensed state, while the hotter one comes from a smaller region covered by an atmosphere.
item.dc:creator: Roberto Taverna, Lorenzo Marra, Roberto Turolla, Ruth M. E. Kelly, Silvia Zane, Alice Borghese, Francesco Coti Zelati, Paolo Esposito, Gian Luca Israel, Nanda Rea, Haonan Yang, Yilong Wang

item.title: Resistive alignment of a black-hole magnetosphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.13288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Recent numerical simulations have shown that black-hole magnetospheres evolve rapidly toward alignment between the magnetic axis and spin axis but the physical origin of this process has remained unclear. We develop an analytic theory of this alignment within resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics. Taking the slow-spin Blandford-Znajek monopole solution as the exterior magnetic field, we reduce the induction equation to a relaxation equation for the current-sheet inclination angle. Our analysis shows that alignment results from second-order spin effects in the Blandford-Znajek solution combined with explicit resistive dissipation. We test this prediction using resistive-GRMHD simulations at several spins and resistivities and compare the measured late-time secular decay with the analytic prediction. This alignment timescale hence carries a unique signature which combines plasma dissipation with spacetime rotation.
item.dc:creator: Ruben Lier, Oliver Porth

item.title: Cracking Gravitational Wave Multiple Ringdown Modes in Space
item.description: arXiv:2604.20914v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Ringdown signals from perturbed black holes (BHs) offer a clean window into BH spacetime, strong-field gravity, and fundamental physics. Presently the quasi-normal modes of stellar-mass BH ringdowns have been successfully extracted in the ground-based gravitational wave (GW) observations. Looking ahead, the future space-borne observatories will listen to the ringdowns from massive BH binary coalescences more loudly and resolve multiple modes to unprecedented precision, which calls for efficient approaches to mitigate the sharply increasing computational burden. We develop a practical ringdown analysis pipeline for space-borne detectors by implementing FIREFLY, a novel acceleration algorithm validated in ground-based detectors, and for the first time demonstrate its compatibility and effectiveness with the time-delay interferometry (TDI) observables. With high fidelity, we achieve an over two-order-of-magnitude speedup for a simulated ringdown signal including six modes, providing a viable and scalable route for multi-mode ringdown analysis in the space context. This new approach has sound statistical interpretation and is extensible to other GW sources in band.
item.dc:creator: Ziming Wang, Han Wang, Yuxin Yang, Yiming Dong, Hai-Tian Wang, Yi-Ming Hu, Lijing Shao

item.title: The Effect of Mass Loss and Convective Overshooting on the Pre-Collapse Structure, Composition, and Neutrino Emission of Red Supergiants
item.description: arXiv:2604.22605v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Prior to core collapse, the neutrino emission from red supergiants (RSGs) is so large that a nearby ($\lesssim1\:$kpc) RSG will become visible in current and near-future neutrino detectors. The rate of emission and the spectra of the pre-supernova (pre-SN) neutrinos from RSGs are sensitive to the temperature, density, and detailed isotopic composition of the core. During the last year of the star's life, these properties change considerably as the nuclear burning accelerates and deleptonization begins. Uncertainties in stellar evolution modeling - including the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting - alter the thermal conditions and composition of the RSG core as it approaches collapse, and thus one expects a consequent effect upon the pre-SN emission. In this paper we present the first study of how varying the treatment of mass loss and convective overshooting together affects the pre-collapse core properties and neutrino emission of RSGs. We use the stellar evolution instrument MESA and construct a grid of 32 RSG models with zero-age main sequence masses of $\{ 12, 15, 18, 20\}$ M$_\odot$, apply the so-called "Dutch" mass-loss scheme with wind efficiencies of $\{0.2, 0.4, 0.8, 1.0\}$, and consider two convective overshooting schemes. Our models use a large 206-isotope nuclear network in order to accurately compute the structure and composition of the star. We find that varying the treatment of mass loss and overshooting results in significant differences in core properties and the strength and timing of shell burning episodes, and that the onset of silicon shell burning leads to a localized peak in the pre-SN neutrino event rate observed by a JUNO-like detector $\sim 10$ hours to $\sim 1$ hour prior to collapse.
item.dc:creator: McKenzie A. Myers, Claire B. Campbell, Kelly M. Patton, Segev BenZvi, Marta Colomer Molla, Alec Habig, James P. Kneller, Dan Milisavljevic, Jeffrey Tseng

item.title: FRANZ: Framework for analytical one-zone blastwave dynamics
item.description: arXiv:2607.04901v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: (abridged) We develop a flexible analytical framework for modeling blastwave evolution in arbitrary environments and use it to investigate how large-scale galactic structure affects the dynamics and morphology of evolved SNRs and SBs. We introduce FRANZ (FRamework for ANalytical one-Zone blastwave dynamics), a modular thin-shell model that follows the local evolution of a shock-surface segment in environments characterized by arbitrary density, velocity and gravitational fields. After validating the model against well-established analytical results, we apply it to study the effects of vertical stratification, galactic shear and dense galactic substructure on blastwave evolution. FRANZ reproduces the classical evolution of blastwaves in uniform media while extending to complex environments. We derive criteria for disk break out in stratified media, characterize the timescales on which differential rotation deforms blastwaves and identify a new mechanism, by which it can suppress the momentum coupling in continuously-driven blastwaves. Interactions with dense filaments modify both shock-surface morphology and dynamics and confound the interpretation of the expansion history of observed remnants, which depends on the density distribution prior to the onset of explosions, which is fundamentally inaccessible from the observed state. In highly structured media with a high volume-filling factor of diffuse gas, ages inferred from the observed state may be systematically overestimated. FRANZ provides a computationally inexpensive and extensible framework for studying blastwaves in realistic galactic environments. It offers a useful complement to numerical simulations for interpreting observations of evolved SNRs and SBs and for developing improved models of stellar feedback in large-scale simulations.
item.dc:creator: Leonard E. C. Romano
